images.title: Altitude outside the triangle
images.purpose: Show that in a triangle with an obtuse angle at B the altitude from A lands outside, on the extended base.
images.composition: A wide obtuse triangle in the right half, with the extended base running left to a foot below A; generous white space.
exact_structure: Triangle ABC with B at the lower middle-left and C at the lower right on a horizontal base, angle at B obtuse (120°, marked with a small amber #E69F00 arc), A above and to the left of B.
The base BC extended leftwards past B as a dashed grey (#6B7280) line ending at D, directly below A.
A reddish purple (#CC79A7) solid segment AD from A straight down to D on the dashed line.
A small square right-angle mark at D, labelled 90°.
The triangle sides in teal (#0072B2); D lies outside the triangle.
The word outside sits in small text beside D, to show D is outside the triangle.
rejection: the foot D lying between B and C
AD drawn slanted instead of at 90° to the dashed line
images.takeaway: In an obtuse triangle the altitude meets the extended base, outside the triangle.
images.description: An obtuse triangle ABC with the altitude AD falling outside, on the extended base.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Ask where D is compared with the triangle, then why the base had to be extended.

image_decisions.why: Different from the acute case: the foot of the altitude is on the extension.
